94243.q: What happens if you are around the same smell for a long time?
a: You hardly smell it any more
You smell it more and more strongly
94243.e: The nose gets used to a smell that stays for a long time. That is why you hardly notice the smell of your own home.
94243.m: The nose gets used to smells that stay the same.

94244.q: Which animal helps to find truffles in the ground?
94244.e: Truffles are mushrooms under the ground. Pigs and specially trained dogs can smell them through the soil.
94244.m: Pigs can smell truffles under the ground.

94245.q: What is the sense we use to notice smells called?
94245.e: With our sense of smell we notice scents and stinks. It is one of our five senses.
94245.m: We notice smells with our sense of smell.

94246.q: Why do homes need smoke alarms?
a: When asleep you hardly smell smoke
Smoke smells of nothing at all
Smoke alarms put out the fire
94246.e: Someone who is asleep is usually not woken by the smell of smoke. But the loud alarm of the smoke alarm wakes you up.
94246.m: When you are asleep, the smoke alarm warns you instead of your nose.

94247.q: What have you got when your nose is runny and blocked?
94247.e: With a cold, the inside of the nose is inflamed. It makes a lot of mucus and swells up.
94247.m: With a cold, your nose runs or gets blocked.

94248.q: What usually causes an ordinary cold?
94248.e: A cold is usually caused by viruses. They are passed on when people sneeze, for example.
94248.m: A cold is mostly caused by viruses.

94249.q: Where does a used tissue belong?
94249.e: There are germs in a used tissue. That is why you throw it away and wash your hands afterwards.
94249.m: A used tissue goes in the bin.

94250.q: How long does an ordinary cold usually last?
94250.e: A simple cold usually goes away by itself after about a week.
94250.m: A cold usually goes away after about a week.

94251.q: What helps so that you do not pass your cold on to others?
94251.e: Germs often stick to our hands. We wash them away with water and soap.
94251.m: Washing your hands protects against infection.

94252.q: Does an antibiotic help against an ordinary cold?
a: Yes, straight away after an hour
Yes, but only in the evening
Yes, if you rub it on your nose
94252.e: Antibiotics only work against bacteria. An ordinary cold goes away by itself without them.
94252.m: Antibiotics do not help against an ordinary cold.

a: A cold that only happens in winter
94253.e: With hay fever, the body reacts to the dust from flowers, which is called pollen. Your nose runs and your eyes itch.
94253.m: Hay fever is an allergy to pollen.

94254.q: What does you good when you have a cold?
a: Lots of ice cream and running
94254.e: With a cold, rest and plenty to drink help, for example warm tea. That way the body can recover.
94254.m: With a cold, rest and warm drinks help.

94255.q: What should you never put into a nostril?
94255.e: Small things like beads or peas can get stuck in the nose. Then a doctor often has to help.
94255.m: Small objects do not belong in the nose.

94256.q: What are the two openings in a horse's nose called?
94256.e: Horses and cattle breathe through their nostrils. They can open them very wide.
94256.m: Horses can open their nostrils wide.

94257.q: Which animal has its nostrils at the tip of a long trunk?
94257.e: An elephant's trunk is a very long nose. Right at the front are the two nostrils.
94257.m: The trunk is the elephant's nose.

94258.q: What is the space behind the nostrils called?
94258.e: Air flows through the nostrils into the nasal cavity. From there it goes on into the throat.
94258.m: Behind the nostrils is the nasal cavity.

94259.q: Why is a dog's nose usually damp around the nostrils?
a: So that it can see better
Because it always has a cold
So that it barks more quietly
94259.e: Scent particles stick well to the damp skin around the nostrils. That way the dog can notice smells even better.
94259.m: A damp dog's nose helps with smelling.

94260.q: Which bird has its nostrils right at the tip of its beak?
94260.e: The kiwi from New Zealand has its nostrils at the tip of its long beak. That way it smells worms in the ground.
94260.m: The kiwi smells with the tip of its beak.

94261.q: Which animal can close its nostrils when diving?
94261.e: Hippos spend a lot of time in water. When they go under, they close their nostrils so no water runs in.
94261.m: Hippos close their nostrils when they dive.

a: On top of the tip of the snout
94262.e: A crocodile's nostrils are on top of its snout. That way it can breathe while lying almost completely under water.
94262.m: Crocodiles breathe through nostrils on top of the snout.

94263.q: How many basic tastes are known today?
94263.e: The five basic tastes are sweet, sour, salty, bitter and umami. Everything else is a mixture or comes from smelling.

94264.q: Is it true that each part of the tongue only tastes one flavour?
a: No, all parts taste all the basic tastes
Yes, only sweet at the front and only bitter at the back
Yes, only the middle tastes anything
Yes, only the edges taste anything
94264.e: The old tongue map is wrong. All the basic tastes can be detected all over the tongue.
94264.m: The whole tongue tastes all the basic tastes.

94265.q: Is “spicy”, like chilli, a basic taste?
a: No, it is a feeling of pain and heat
Yes, it is the sixth basic taste
Yes, it is a kind of sweet
Yes, it is a kind of salty
94265.e: The substance in chilli irritates nerves that report heat and pain. That is why spicy food feels like burning.
94265.m: Spicy is a feeling of pain, not a taste.

94266.q: What does food need so that the tongue can taste it?
94266.e: Saliva dissolves the taste substances from the food. Only then can the taste buds recognise them.

94267.q: Which animal tastes with its feet?
94267.e: Butterflies have sensory cells on their feet. When they land on a flower, they can taste straight away whether there is food there.

94268.q: Which fish has taste cells over almost all of its skin?
94268.e: Catfish have taste cells all over their body. That way they find their food in murky water.
94268.m: The catfish tastes with almost all of its skin.

94269.q: Why does very cold ice cream taste less sweet than melted ice cream?
a: Cold makes the tongue less sensitive
94269.e: When it is very cold, the tongue senses sweetness less strongly. That is why melted ice cream often tastes much sweeter.

94270.e: Cats lack the sensory cell for sweet. They mainly eat meat and do not need sugar.

94271.e: Sugar tastes sweet. It is found in fruit, honey and sweets.

94272.q: Which taste do even babies especially like?
94272.e: Even babies like sweet things, and breast milk tastes slightly sweet too.
94272.m: Even babies like the sweet taste.

94273.q: What does a sweet taste tell the body?
94273.e: Sweet food contains sugar, and sugar provides energy. That is why our body likes sweet things.
94273.m: Sweet shows that there is energy in the food.

94274.q: Why should you brush your teeth after eating sweets?
a: So that your tongue gets sweeter
94274.e: Bacteria in the mouth turn sugar into acid. This acid can make holes in the teeth, called tooth decay.
94274.m: Brushing your teeth after sweet things protects against tooth decay.

94275.q: Which fruit tastes especially sweet when ripe?
94275.e: Ripe bananas contain a lot of sugar, so they taste sweet.

94276.q: How does the taste of a fruit change when it ripens?
94276.e: As it ripens, the fruit makes more sugar. Unripe fruit often tastes sour or tart.
94276.m: Ripe fruit tastes sweeter than unripe fruit.

94277.q: Which sweet syrup is made from the sap of a tree?
94277.e: Maple syrup is made from the sap of the sugar maple. The sap is boiled until a sweet syrup is left.
94277.m: Maple syrup comes from the sap of the maple tree.

94278.q: From which tall grass plant is sugar made in warm countries?
94278.e: Sugar cane is a tall grass with sweet juice. A lot of sugar is made from it in warm countries.
94278.m: Sugar cane is a sweet grass.

94279.q: Which liquid from the kitchen tastes sour?
94279.e: Vinegar contains acetic acid, which is why it tastes sour. It is used in salad dressing, for example.

94280.e: Sour food contains acid, such as citric acid or acetic acid. The tongue recognises this acid.

94281.q: What does milk that has gone off taste like?
94281.e: When milk gets old, bacteria turn the milk sugar into acid. That is why it tastes sour.
94281.m: Milk that has gone off tastes sour.

94282.q: Which dairy product tastes slightly sour?
94282.e: Yoghurt is made with bacteria that produce lactic acid. That is why yoghurt tastes slightly sour.
94282.m: Yoghurt tastes slightly sour because of lactic acid.

94283.q: Which vegetable is used for sauerkraut?
94283.e: Sauerkraut is made from finely cut white cabbage. As it ferments, lactic acid forms and makes it sour.
94283.m: Sauerkraut is made from white cabbage.

94284.q: What can a sour taste warn you about?
94284.e: Unripe fruit and spoiled food often taste sour. That way you notice that something is not good.
94284.m: Sour can warn of something unripe or spoiled.

94285.q: What face do many people pull when they bite into a lemon?
a: They screw up their eyes and mouth
94285.e: The strong sour taste makes many people pull a face. Their eyes and mouth get screwed up.
94285.m: Many people pull a face at sour things.

94286.q: Which green citrus fruit tastes very sour?
94286.e: The lime is related to the lemon. Its juice contains a lot of acid and tastes very sour.

94287.q: What do crisps usually taste like?
94287.e: Crisps are seasoned with salt. That is why they taste salty.

94288.q: Which seasoning do you sprinkle on a breakfast egg to make it taste salty?
94288.e: Table salt tastes salty. Many people sprinkle a pinch of it on a boiled egg.

94290.q: Why does our body need a little salt?
a: So that nerves and muscles work well
94290.e: Salt contains sodium, which nerves and muscles need. But too much salt is unhealthy.
94290.m: The body needs a little salt, but not too much.

94291.q: What tastes salty when it runs down your face?
94291.e: Tears contain a little salt. That is why they taste slightly salty.

94292.q: Why is salt spread on the roads in winter?
a: So that the road gets clean
So that the road gets warm
94292.e: Salt makes ice and snow melt. That way roads and pavements are less slippery.
94292.m: Road salt makes ice on the road melt.

94293.q: What does eating a lot of salty food often give you?
94293.e: Salt holds on to water in the body. That is why the body signals thirst after salty food.

94294.q: What does coffee without sugar taste like?
94294.e: Coffee contains bitter substances such as caffeine. Without sugar it therefore tastes bitter.

94295.q: What does a bitter taste often warn us about?
94295.e: Many poisonous plants taste bitter. That is why people often prefer to spit out bitter things.

94296.q: Which chocolate tastes the most bitter?
94296.e: Dark chocolate has a lot of cocoa and little sugar. Cocoa tastes bitter.
94296.m: Dark chocolate tastes more bitter than milk chocolate.

94297.q: Which vegetable often tastes a little bitter?
94297.e: Chicory contains bitter substances. That is why many children like it less.

94298.q: Why do children often like bitter things less than adults?
a: Children cannot taste bitterness at all
Bitter things are only poisonous for children
94298.e: Children react more strongly to bitterness than adults. As they get older, many get used to bitter food.

94299.q: What does the white pith under orange peel taste like?
94299.e: The white pith of an orange contains bitter substances. That is why people often pick it off.
94299.m: The white pith of an orange tastes bitter.

94300.q: Which drink made from leaves can turn bitter if it brews too long?
94300.e: If black tea brews for too long, a lot of tannins dissolve. Then it tastes bitter.
94300.m: Tea that brews too long turns bitter.

94301.q: Apart from sour, what does a grapefruit taste like?
94301.e: Grapefruits contain bitter substances. So they taste bitter and also a bit sour.

94302.q: Which red salad leaf tastes slightly bitter?
94302.e: Radicchio has red leaves with white veins. It contains bitter substances, so it tastes slightly bitter.

94303.q: Which basic taste has a name that roughly means “delicious”?
94303.e: Umami roughly means delicious. It describes a strong, savoury taste.

94304.q: Which country does the word “umami” come from?
94304.e: The Japanese scientist Kikunae Ikeda described the taste umami in 1908. He found it in a seaweed soup.
94304.m: The word umami comes from Japan.

94305.e: Stock tastes strong and savoury. This taste is called umami.

94306.q: Which cheese has a strong umami taste?
94306.e: Cheese that has matured for a long time, like Parmesan, tastes very savoury. It has a lot of umami.
94306.m: Mature cheese like Parmesan tastes umami.

94307.q: What is the substance that gives many foods their umami taste called?
94307.e: Glutamate is found naturally in many foods. The tongue has sensory cells that recognise it as umami.

94308.q: Which sauce from Asia tastes strongly umami?
94308.e: Soy sauce is made from soya beans and matured for a long time. It tastes salty and very umami.

94309.q: Which vegetable tastes especially umami when ripe and dried?
94309.e: Ripe and dried tomatoes contain a lot of the substance that tastes umami. That is why they flavour sauces so well.

94310.q: Which savoury spread from Switzerland tastes strongly umami?
94310.e: Cenovis is a savoury paste made from brewer's yeast that you spread on bread and butter. Yeast extract tastes strongly umami.
94310.m: Cenovis is a savoury Swiss yeast spread.

94311.q: Where are most of the taste buds?
94311.e: Most taste buds are on the tongue. Only a few are in other places in the mouth.
94311.m: Most taste buds are on the tongue.

94312.q: What are the little bumps on the tongue that contain taste buds called?
94312.e: The rough tongue is covered in little bumps called papillae. Many of them contain taste buds.
94312.m: Taste buds sit in the papillae of the tongue.

94313.q: Roughly how many taste buds does a person have?
94313.e: A person has several thousand taste buds. Each one is made up of many sensory cells.
94313.m: A person has a few thousand taste buds.

94314.q: What happens to the sensory cells in the taste buds after a while?
a: They are replaced by new ones
94314.e: The sensory cells only live a short time, about one to two weeks. Then new ones grow.
94314.m: Taste cells are renewed again and again.

94315.q: What often happens when you burn your tongue on hot tea?
a: You taste less for a while
You cannot smell anything any more
94315.e: Heat can injure the sensory cells on the tongue. Until new ones have grown, you taste less.
94315.m: A burnt tongue tastes less for a while.

94316.q: What does the surface of the tongue feel like?
94316.e: The many papillae make the tongue rough. The taste buds are in them too.
94316.m: The tongue is rough because of the papillae.

94317.q: What connects the taste buds to the brain?
94317.e: The sensory cells send their message along nerves to the brain. There the feeling of sweet or bitter is created.
94317.m: Nerves carry taste to the brain.

94318.q: Apart from the tongue, where else are there some taste buds?
a: On the roof of the mouth and in the throat
94318.e: Some taste buds are on the roof of the mouth and in the throat. But most are on the tongue.
94318.m: There are taste buds on the roof of the mouth too.

94319.e: A scent is a smell that we find pleasant. One example is the smell of flowers.
94319.m: A scent is a pleasant smell.

94320.q: Which purple plant smells strongly and is often put into scented bags?
94320.e: Lavender has purple flowers and a strong scent. Dried, it is put in little bags in the wardrobe.

94321.q: Why do many flowers have a scent?
94321.e: The scent attracts bees and other insects. As they visit, they carry pollen from flower to flower.

94322.q: What can you often smell in the morning at the baker's?
94322.e: Baking produces lots of scents. That is why the baker's smells of fresh bread.

94323.q: What is a scented liquid you spray on your skin called?
94323.e: Perfume contains scents from flowers, woods or the laboratory. You spray it on to smell nice.

94324.q: Where do scent particles have to go for us to smell them?
94324.e: Scent particles float in the air. We breathe them in, and the smell cells in the nose recognise them.
94324.m: Scent particles travel through the air into the nose.

94325.q: What can scents easily bring back?
94325.e: In the brain, smells quickly reach the areas for feelings and memories. That is why a scent often reminds you of the past.

94326.q: Which flower is famous for its scent and often has thorns on its stem?
94326.e: Many roses smell strongly and have thorns on the stem. Rose oil is also made from their petals.
94326.m: Roses are known for their scent.

94327.q: Why do you smell less outside in winter than in summer?
a: The nose is smaller in winter
There is no air in winter
The smell cells sleep in winter
94327.e: When it is warm, scents evaporate faster and drift through the air. In the cold there are fewer scent particles.
94327.m: Warmth spreads scents better than cold.

94328.e: A stink is a smell that we find disgusting. It often warns us about something bad.
94328.m: A stink is an unpleasant smell.

94329.q: Which animal sprays a smelly liquid when in danger?
94329.e: The skunk lives in America. When in danger, it sprays a very foul-smelling liquid at its enemies.
94329.m: The skunk defends itself with a stink.

94330.q: What does the stink of spoiled food warn us about?
a: That it is about to rain
94330.e: Spoiled food smells bad because bacteria are growing in it. Anyone who eats it can get ill.
94330.m: You should not eat food that stinks.

94331.q: What does natural gas smell of, so that a leak is noticed straight away?
a: A smelly substance that is added
94331.e: Natural gas itself hardly smells. That is why a strong-smelling substance is added, so that you smell a leak straight away.
94331.m: Natural gas is given a smell so that leaks are noticed.

94332.q: What do rotten eggs smell of?
94332.e: Rotten eggs give off a gas that contains sulphur. It smells very unpleasant.

94333.q: Which insect gives off a foul smell when disturbed?
94333.e: Stink bugs release a foul-smelling liquid when in danger. That way they scare off enemies.
94333.m: Stink bugs protect themselves with a stink.

94334.q: What should you do if your home smells of gas?
a: Open the windows and go outside
94334.e: Gas can burn or explode. That is why you let in air, leave the home and call for help outside.
94334.m: If you smell gas, let in air and go outside.

94335.q: Which giant flower stinks of rotting meat?
94335.e: The titan arum has one of the largest flower heads in the world. Its stink attracts flies and beetles that pollinate it.
94335.m: The titan arum attracts insects with its stink.

95126.q: Which sense tells you whether something is rough or smooth?
95126.e: With the sense of touch you feel what a surface is like. You need neither eyes nor ears for it.
95126.m: With the sense of touch you feel rough and smooth.

95127.q: Where on the hand are there especially many touch receptors?
a: On the back of the hand
95127.e: There are a great many tiny sensors in the fingertips. That is why you can feel things especially finely with them.

95128.q: What do ants use to feel their way?
95128.e: Ants touch the ground and other ants with their movable antennae. They can also smell with them.

95129.q: Which part of its body does an elephant use to feel things especially finely?
95129.e: The tip of an elephant's trunk is very sensitive. With it, the elephant can even feel and grab small things like a peanut.
95129.m: An elephant feels things with its trunk.

95130.q: What do you say about someone who does a difficult thing very carefully and skilfully?
95130.e: Having a delicate touch means being sensitive and skilful. The phrase comes from the fine sense of touch in the fingers.
95130.m: Someone who is skilful and sensitive has a delicate touch.

95131.q: Where do the nerves report what the fingers feel?
95131.e: The nerves carry the messages from the skin to the brain in a flash. Only there do you notice what you are touching.
95131.m: The brain processes what the skin feels.

95132.q: What do babies very often use to feel objects?
95132.e: Lips and tongue can feel very finely. That is why babies put lots of things in their mouth to explore them.
95132.m: Babies often explore things with their mouth.

95133.q: What can you find out by touch with your eyes closed?
a: Whether something is soft or hard
95133.e: When you touch something, you feel whether it gives way or is firm. Colours and brightness, on the other hand, can only be seen.
95133.m: By touch you feel whether something is soft or hard.

95134.q: What do cats use to feel their surroundings in the dark?
95134.e: A cat's whiskers are very sensitive. They can feel even tiny movements of air and narrow gaps.

95135.q: What does a glowing sign on a switched-off hob mean?
95135.e: Even after it is switched off, a hob stays hot for a long time. The display warns you not to touch it.
95135.m: A heat warning light warns of a hot hob.

95136.q: What do you call a lightning-fast movement of the body that happens without thinking?
95136.e: In a reflex, the body reacts by itself and very quickly. This protects us from injuries.
95136.m: A reflex is a movement without thinking.

95137.q: What do you use to hold a hot pan?
95137.e: A thick oven glove only lets the heat through slowly. That way you do not burn your hands.
95137.m: You hold hot pans with an oven glove.

95138.q: What does the body do in great heat to cool down?
95138.e: Sweat comes out of the skin and evaporates. This makes the skin cooler.
95138.m: In the heat, the body cools down by sweating.

95139.q: Which part of the body do parents often use to check that a baby's bath water is not too hot?
95139.e: The skin on the elbow is thinner and less used to heat than the palm of the hand. So you can easily tell whether the water feels pleasant.
95139.m: You check the warmth of bath water with your elbow.

95140.q: What does your skin get if you stay in the sun too long without protection?
95140.e: The sun's rays damage the skin. It turns red, hot and painful. Sun cream and shade protect you.
95140.m: Too much sun gives you sunburn.

95141.q: What can form on the skin when you burn yourself?
95141.e: With a burn, fluid collects under the skin. This forms a blister, which you should not burst.
95141.m: A burn can cause a blister.

95142.q: Why should you not walk barefoot over hot tarmac in summer?
a: You can burn the soles of your feet
It makes you tired straight away
95142.e: Dark tarmac gets very hot in the sun. The skin on the soles of your feet can get burnt.
95142.m: Hot tarmac can burn the soles of your feet.

95143.q: What do you get on your skin when you are cold?
95143.e: In the cold, the tiny hairs stand up and the skin forms little bumps. In Switzerland people call this “chicken skin”.
95143.m: When you are cold, you get goose bumps.

95144.q: What does the body do to make heat when it is very cold?
95144.e: When you shiver, your muscles move very fast. This makes heat.
95144.m: Shivering warms the body in the cold.

95145.q: Which parts of the body usually get cold first?
95145.e: In the cold, the body sends warm blood mainly to the important organs. That is why fingers and toes get cold quickly.
95145.m: Fingers and toes get cold first.

95146.q: What is an injury to the skin caused by extreme cold called?
95146.e: In extreme cold, the skin on fingers, toes, ears or nose can be damaged. This is called frostbite.

95147.q: What protects your hands from the cold in winter?
95147.e: Gloves hold the warm air around your hands. That way your fingers do not cool down so quickly.
95147.m: Gloves keep your hands warm in winter.

95148.q: What happens to your hand if you hold an ice cube for a long time?
95148.e: The cold slows down the nerves in the skin. Then you feel almost nothing and your hand goes numb.
95148.m: Great cold makes the skin numb.

95149.q: What do you put on a fresh bump on the head?
95149.e: Cold makes the swelling less bad and eases the pain. Never put ice directly on the skin.

95150.q: Why does a metal railing feel colder in winter than a wooden one?
a: Wood is always in the sun
95150.e: Metal takes the warmth from your hand very quickly. That is why it feels colder, even when it is just as cold as the wood.
95150.m: Metal feels cold because it carries heat away quickly.

95151.q: Why is pain useful for the body?
95151.e: Pain is a warning signal. It shows that something is hurting the body or that something is wrong.

95152.q: What is a medicine that eases pain called?
95152.e: A painkiller dulls the pain. Children should only take it when an adult allows it.

95153.q: What does the number 0 mean on a pain scale from 0 to 10?
95153.e: With the pain scale you show the doctor how much something hurts. 0 means no pain, 10 the worst.
95153.m: On the pain scale, 0 means no pain.

95154.q: What is a blue mark that appears after a knock called?
95154.e: When you knock yourself, tiny blood vessels under the skin burst. The blood collects there and shows through blue.
95154.m: A blue mark is a bruise.

95155.q: What do you feel when you knock your funny bone on your elbow?
a: A warm tickle in your tummy
95155.e: At the elbow, a nerve lies right under the skin. If you hit it, it tingles all the way to your fingers.
95155.m: At the funny bone, a nerve lies right under the skin.

95157.q: What usually happens to the skin after a wasp sting?
95157.e: When a wasp stings, it injects a little poison into the skin. The spot turns red, swells and hurts.
95157.m: A wasp sting swells up and hurts.

95158.q: What should you do if a pain does not go away for a long time?
95158.e: Long or strong pain can be a sign of an illness. A doctor can find out where it comes from.
95158.m: With long-lasting pain you go to the doctor.

95159.q: Why can you not really tickle yourself?
a: The brain knows in advance where it will be touched
Your own fingers are too cold
95159.e: The brain plans your own movement and expects the touch. So the surprise is gone and it does not tickle.

95160.q: Where are many people especially ticklish?
a: On the soles of the feet
On the top of the head
95160.e: There are many sensitive nerves on the soles of the feet. A light touch there tickles many people a lot.
95160.m: Many people are ticklish on the soles of their feet.

95161.q: What do most people do when they are tickled?
95161.e: Tickling makes most people laugh. That happens even though it is not always pleasant.
95161.m: Most people laugh when they are tickled.

95162.q: Which animals make a laughing sound when tickled?
95162.e: Young chimpanzees and other great apes also pant when tickled, as if they were laughing. This is how they play together.

95163.q: What often makes you sneeze when your nose tickles?
95163.e: Dust irritates the lining of the nose. By sneezing, the body blasts it back out.
95163.m: Dust in the nose makes you sneeze.

95164.q: What should you do if someone says “Stop” while you are tickling them?
95164.e: Tickling can become unpleasant. Anyone who says stop must be taken seriously.
95164.m: If someone says stop, you stop.

95165.q: What do you feel when an ant crawls over your arm?
95165.e: Its little legs touch the fine hairs on the skin. You feel this as a light tingling or tickling.
95165.m: A crawling ant tingles on the skin.

95166.e: Blind people and people with very poor sight can read Braille. They do not need their eyes for it.

95167.q: What can you use to write Braille?
95167.e: A Braille writing machine presses the dots into thick paper from below. Today there are also printers for it.
95167.m: Braille is written with a Braille writing machine.

95168.q: How did Louis Braille become blind as a small child?
a: Through an accident in the workshop
Through a fall from a horse
95168.e: At about three years old, he hurt his eye with a sharp tool in his father's workshop. Later he went blind in both eyes.
95168.m: Louis Braille went blind through an accident.

95169.q: Where did Louis Braille hurt his eye as a small child?
95169.e: At about three years old, he was playing with a sharp tool in his father's workshop. He hurt his eye and later went completely blind.
95169.m: Louis Braille hurt himself in his father's workshop.

95170.q: Why are books in Braille much thicker than other books?
a: The dots take up a lot of space
The paper is made of wood
95170.e: The dots must be big enough to feel. That is why much less text fits on a page.
95170.m: Books in Braille are very thick.

95171.q: Roughly how old was Louis Braille when he invented his dot writing?
95171.e: Louis Braille finished his dot writing in 1825. He was only 16 years old at the time.
95171.m: Louis Braille was still a teenager when he invented the writing.

95172.q: Which writing for soldiers gave Louis Braille his idea?
a: A writing for reading in the dark
A writing made of smoke signals
95172.e: An army officer had invented a night writing made of raised dots. Braille turned it into a simpler writing.
95172.m: A night writing for soldiers gave Braille his idea.

95173.q: What do the signs of Braille feel like?
95173.e: The dots are pressed out of the paper. You feel them as little raised bumps.
95173.m: The dots of Braille stand out from the paper.

95174.q: What do you do on a barefoot trail?
95174.e: On a barefoot trail you take off your shoes and socks. With your bare feet you feel the ground.
95174.m: On a barefoot trail you walk without shoes.

95175.q: What do you feel with your feet on a barefoot trail?
95175.e: A barefoot trail goes over grass, sand, stones, bark or mud. Each surface feels different.
95175.m: On a barefoot trail you feel different surfaces.

95176.q: Which surface feels especially soft on a barefoot trail?
95176.e: Moss is a soft, damp cushion of tiny plants. Walking on it feels like walking on a carpet.
95176.m: Moss feels soft under your feet.

95177.q: Which surface prickles most under your feet?
95177.e: Fir cones are hard and spiky. Walking on them prickles the soles of your feet.
95177.m: Fir cones prickle under your feet.

95178.q: What should you do after a barefoot trail?
95178.e: After a barefoot trail your feet are often dirty. That is why many barefoot trails have a basin for washing at the end.
95178.m: After a barefoot trail you wash your feet.

95179.q: What gets especially strong when you walk barefoot?
95179.e: Without shoes, the small muscles in the foot work harder. That keeps the feet strong and flexible.
95179.m: Walking barefoot strengthens the foot muscles.

95180.q: In which canton is the well-known barefoot trail from Jakobsbad to Gontenbad?
95180.e: The barefoot trail runs through the hilly countryside near Gonten in the Appenzell region. It is a few kilometres long.
95180.m: A well-known barefoot trail is in the Appenzell region.

95181.q: Why is the grass often wet early in the morning?
95181.e: In the cool night, tiny drops of water from the air form on the grass. This is the dew.
95181.m: In the morning the grass is wet with dew.

95182.q: In which season do people most like going on a barefoot trail?
95182.e: In summer the ground is warm and pleasant. In winter and cool times it would be too cold for bare feet.
95182.m: Barefoot trails are best in summer.

95183.q: What do you do with a feely box?
95183.e: You reach into the box through a hole. You have to guess what is inside only by touch.
95183.m: In a feely box you recognise things by touch.

95184.q: Which parts of the body do you use most with a feely box?
95184.e: The objects are hidden so you cannot see them. You only recognise them by grabbing and feeling them.
95184.m: With a feely box you recognise things with your hands.

95185.q: What does a fir cone feel like in the feely box?
95185.e: A fir cone has lots of hard, scale-like parts. You can feel the edges well with your fingers.
95185.m: A fir cone feels rough and scaly.

95186.q: Which object feels soft and fluffy?
95186.e: Cotton wool is made of many fine fibres with air in between. That is why it is soft and fluffy.
95186.m: Cotton wool feels soft and fluffy.

95187.q: Which object feels smooth and cool?
95187.e: A metal spoon has no grooves and no fibres. It feels smooth and cool.
95187.m: A metal spoon feels smooth and cool.

95188.q: How do you recognise a walnut in the feely box?
a: It is hard with a wrinkly shell
95188.e: The shell of a walnut is hard and has lots of grooves. You can feel that well with your fingers.
95188.m: A walnut has a hard, wrinkly shell.

95189.q: Which object is soft, has lots of holes and soaks up water?
95189.e: A sponge is full of tiny holes. You can squeeze it and it takes in water.
95189.m: A sponge is soft and full of holes.

95190.q: Why should nothing sharp go into a feely box?
a: So that the box is lighter
So that you can see more
95190.e: You reach into the box without looking. Pointed or sharp things could hurt your hands.
95190.m: Nothing sharp goes into a feely box.

95191.q: What do you do almost automatically when something itches?
95191.e: An itch makes you want to scratch. Scratching helps for a moment, but it can irritate the skin.
95191.m: When something itches, you want to scratch.

95192.q: What itches for many people in spring when pollen is in the air?
95192.e: With hay fever, the body reacts to pollen. Then your eyes and nose itch and you have to sneeze.
95192.m: With hay fever, pollen makes your eyes and nose itch.

95193.q: Which plant stings and itches on the skin when you touch it?
95193.e: The stinging nettle has fine stinging hairs. When you touch them, they break off and release a burning juice into the skin. Small red bumps then appear that itch.
95193.m: The stinging nettle stings and itches on the skin.

95194.q: What often itches when a graze is healing?
95194.e: New skin grows under the scab. This often itches, but you should not pick off the scab.

95195.q: What can happen if you scratch a mosquito bite until it bleeds?
95195.e: Scratching gets dirt and germs into the little wound. Then it can get infected.

95196.q: Which small creatures can make your head itch and turn up in school classes?
95196.e: Head lice live in the hair. Their bites itch, and they do not jump but crawl from head to head.
95196.m: Head lice make your head itch.

95197.q: Which childhood illness causes lots of itchy blisters all over the body?
95197.e: With chickenpox, lots of small, itchy blisters appear on the skin. In Switzerland it is also called “Wilde Blattern”.

95198.q: What helps against dry, itchy skin in winter?
95198.e: A good cream keeps the skin moist and soft. Then it itches less.
95198.m: Putting cream on helps against dry skin.

95199.q: What do you feel when a shoe is too small?
95199.e: If a shoe is too small, it presses on your toes and foot. You feel this as unpleasant pressure.
95199.m: A shoe that is too small pinches.

95200.q: How do you check with your thumb whether a bicycle tyre has enough air?
95200.e: A well-pumped tyre hardly gives when you press it. If it is soft, it needs more air.
95200.m: By pressing, you check whether a tyre has enough air.

95201.q: What do you feel in your ears when you dive deep in the swimming pool?
95201.e: The deeper you dive, the more water presses down from above. You feel this especially in your ears.
95201.m: When diving, you feel pressure in your ears.

95202.q: What does a sock top that is too tight leave on your skin?
95202.e: The elastic presses into the skin for a long time. Afterwards you see red lines that soon disappear.
95202.m: Tight socks leave marks on the skin.

95203.q: What does the doctor measure with an inflatable cuff on the upper arm?
95203.e: The cuff squeezes the arm for a moment. A device measures how strongly the blood presses against the blood vessels.
95203.m: The cuff is used to measure blood pressure.

95204.q: Why does a pointed stone under your foot hurt more than a flat one?
a: Your weight presses on a small spot
95204.e: With a pointed stone, your whole weight presses on a tiny point. That is why the pressure there is very great.
95204.m: On a small area the pressure is especially great.

95205.q: What do you do with a clean cloth when a wound is bleeding heavily?
a: Press it firmly on the wound
Put it next to the wound
95205.e: Pressure on the wound slows the bleeding. Then you quickly get help.
95205.m: You press a clean cloth on a bleeding wound.

95206.q: What do you feel when the phone buzzes in your trouser pocket?
95206.e: Inside the phone, a tiny motor spins very fast. The device shakes and you feel it on your skin.

95207.q: What vibrates in your throat when you hum?
95207.e: When you hum, the vocal cords in the voice box vibrate. If you put your hand on your throat, you can feel the trembling.
95207.m: When you hum, your vocal cords vibrate.

95208.q: What do you feel under your feet when a heavy lorry drives past close by?
95208.e: The heavy lorry makes the ground vibrate. You feel this vibration with your feet.
95208.m: Heavy vehicles make the ground vibrate.

95209.q: What is a device that measures the shaking of earthquakes called?
95209.e: A seismograph records even the smallest movements of the ground. In Switzerland, the Swiss Seismological Service at ETH Zurich does the measuring.

95210.q: How can deaf people feel music?
95210.e: Loud music makes the floor and the air vibrate. Deaf people feel the bass with their whole body.
95210.m: Deaf people feel music through vibrations.

95211.q: What do you feel in your fingers when you pluck a guitar string?
95211.e: The plucked string swings back and forth. This makes the note, and you feel the fine trembling.

95212.q: How does a spider notice that an insect is caught in its web?
95212.e: The trapped insect wriggles and makes the threads vibrate. The spider feels this with its legs.
95212.m: A spider feels prey by the trembling of its web.

95213.q: What do you feel in your hand with an electric toothbrush?
95213.e: In an electric toothbrush, a motor moves the brush head very fast. You feel this as a vibration in your hand.

95214.q: What do people often put in bed in winter to make it warm?
95214.e: A hot-water bottle is filled with warm water. It warms the bed and your feet.
95214.m: A hot-water bottle warms the bed.

95215.q: Which material keeps you especially warm in winter?
95215.e: There is a lot of air trapped between the wool fibres. This air holds on to your body heat.
95215.m: Wool keeps you warm in winter.

95216.q: Which T-shirt gets warmer in the sun?
95216.e: Dark colours absorb more sunlight than light ones. That is why dark clothes get warmer in the sun.
95216.m: Dark clothes get warmer in the sun.

95217.q: Why do you rub your hands together when it is cold?
95217.e: When you rub things against each other, heat is produced. This is called friction heat.

95218.q: Why do emperor penguins stand close together in winter?
95218.e: In Antarctica it is freezing cold. Huddled close together, the penguins lose less heat.

95219.q: What do you feel on your skin when you sit close to a campfire?
95219.e: The fire sends out heat rays. They warm the skin even without you touching the fire.
95219.m: A campfire warms you with heat rays.

95220.q: Why does lukewarm water feel hot on your hands after a snowball fight?
a: Because your hands are very cold
95220.e: The skin compares the temperature with its own. So cold hands feel lukewarm water as hot.
95220.m: Cold hands feel lukewarm water as hot.

95221.q: Which stove heats the living room in many old Swiss farmhouses?
95221.e: A tiled stove stores the heat of the fire in its tiles. It gives it off to the room for a long time.
95221.m: A tiled stove keeps the room warm for a long time.

95222.q: Which colour on a tap usually shows warm water?
95222.e: Red stands for warm and blue for cold. That way you know which way to turn.
95222.m: On a tap, red means warm water.

95223.q: What tickles especially when you stroke it very lightly over the skin?
95223.e: A feather touches the skin only very gently. Many people feel this light touch as tickling.
95223.m: A feather tickles on the skin.

95224.q: What does a dog do with its mouth open to cool down in the heat?
95224.e: When panting, water evaporates from the tongue and mouth. This cools the dog down.

95225.q: What is the capital of the canton of Aargau?
95225.e: Aarau is the capital of the canton of Aargau. The government and the cantonal parliament work there.

95226.q: Which river gives the canton of Aargau its name?
95226.e: The name Aargau roughly means “land on the Aare”. The Aare flows right across the whole canton.
95226.m: Aargau means land on the Aare.

95227.q: Which neighbouring country borders the canton of Aargau to the north?
95227.e: In the north, the Rhine forms the border between Aargau and Germany.
95227.m: Across the Rhine, Aargau looks towards Germany.

95228.q: Which lake is in the canton of Aargau?
95228.e: Lake Hallwil lies in the Seetal valley in the canton of Aargau. In summer you can swim and take boat trips there.
95228.m: Lake Hallwil is the largest lake in Aargau.

95229.q: Which vegetable is in the famous cake from the canton of Aargau?
95229.e: Aargau carrot cake is baked with grated carrots and almonds. It is moist and often decorated with little marzipan carrots.
95229.m: Aargau carrot cake: carrots in the cake.

95230.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Aargau?
95230.e: In the canton of Aargau, German is the official language. In everyday life people speak the Aargau dialect, in other words Swiss German.

95231.q: What is the town of Baden in the canton of Aargau known for?
a: For warm spring water to bathe in
95231.e: In Baden, warm water comes out of the ground. Even the Romans bathed there, which is why the town is called Baden, German for “bathing”.
95231.m: In Baden people bathe in warm spring water.

95232.q: How many white stars are on the coat of arms of the canton of Aargau?
95232.e: The Aargau coat of arms is divided into two halves. On the left is a white river on black, on the right three white stars on blue.
95232.m: Three stars on blue: that is Aargau.

95473.q: What is special about the clock on the Zyt Tower in the Musegg Wall in Lucerne?
a: It may strike one minute before all the other clocks in the city
It has only one hour hand, made of gold
95473.e: The clock in the Zyt Tower is the oldest tower clock in Lucerne. That is why it has the privilege of striking one minute earlier than all the other clocks in the city.
95473.m: The Zyt Tower in Lucerne always strikes first.

95474.q: Which covered wooden bridge in Lucerne is decorated with paintings of a Dance of Death?
95474.e: The Spreuer Bridge is the second old wooden bridge over the Reuss in Lucerne. Its paintings show a Dance of Death from the 17th century.
95474.m: The Spreuer Bridge is the bridge with the Dance of Death.

95475.q: Which river flows out of Lake Lucerne in the city of Lucerne?
95475.e: In Lucerne the Reuss leaves Lake Lucerne. Later, in the canton of Aargau, it flows into the Aare.
95475.m: The Reuss flows right through Lucerne.

95476.q: Which region in the canton of Lucerne is a UNESCO biosphere reserve?
95476.e: The UNESCO Biosphere Entlebuch protects moors, forests and mountains. At the same time, farming and tourism in harmony with nature are encouraged there.
95476.m: The Entlebuch is a UNESCO biosphere.

95477.q: Which of these cantons does NOT border the canton of Lucerne?
95477.e: Lucerne borders Aargau, Zug, Schwyz, Nidwalden, Obwalden and Bern. Uri lies further south and is not a neighbour of Lucerne.
95477.m: Uri is not a neighbour of Lucerne.

95478.q: After the city of Lucerne, which municipality is the largest in the canton of Lucerne?
95478.e: Emmen lies right next to the city of Lucerne and has more than 30,000 inhabitants. That makes it the second-largest municipality in the canton.
95478.m: Emmen is the second-largest municipality in the canton of Lucerne.

95479.q: What is the name of the Lucerne speciality made of puff pastry filled with little meatballs in a cream sauce?
95479.e: The Chügelipastete is a large puff pastry with little meatballs and sauce. It is also called Fritschipastete.
95479.m: People in Lucerne love to eat Chügelipastete.

95480.q: Which modern building right on the lake in Lucerne is world-famous for its concert hall?
95480.e: The KKL (Culture and Convention Centre Lucerne) was designed by the French architect Jean Nouvel. Its large roof sticks out far over the lake.
95480.m: At the KKL Luzern, music sounds out by the lake.

95487.q: What is the capital of the canton of Neuchâtel?
95487.e: The capital is called Neuchâtel, in German Neuenburg. The town lies on Lake Neuchâtel.
95487.m: The canton and its capital are both called Neuchâtel.

95488.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Neuchâtel?
95488.e: People in the canton of Neuchâtel speak French. It belongs to Romandy, the French-speaking part of Switzerland.

95489.q: On which large lake does the town of Neuchâtel lie?
95489.e: The town of Neuchâtel lies on the shore of Lake Neuchâtel. In good weather you can see as far as the Alps from the lake.

95490.q: Which three colours are on the coat of arms of the canton of Neuchâtel?
95490.e: The Neuchâtel coat of arms has three vertical stripes in green, white and red. At the top of the red stripe there is a small white cross.
95490.m: Neuchâtel wears green, white and red.

95491.q: What is the name of the huge rock amphitheatre in the canton of Neuchâtel where you often see ibex?
95491.e: The Creux du Van is an enormous rock bowl with almost vertical walls. Ibex and chamois live there.
95491.m: The Creux du Van is a huge rock amphitheatre.

95492.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Neuchâtel border?
95492.e: The canton of Neuchâtel lies in the Jura and borders France to the west. Part of the border is formed by the river Doubs.
95492.m: Neuchâtel is a neighbour of France.

95493.q: Which big festival does the town of Neuchâtel celebrate every year at the end of September?
a: The Fête des Vendanges (grape harvest festival)
95493.e: At the Fête des Vendanges, Neuchâtel celebrates the end of the grape harvest. There is a big parade with decorated floats and lots of music.
95493.m: At the end of September, Neuchâtel celebrates the Fête des Vendanges.

95494.q: What is the name of the waterfall on the Doubs on the border between the canton of Neuchâtel and France?
95494.e: At the Saut du Doubs, the Doubs plunges about 27 metres. You can reach the waterfall by boat from Les Brenets, for example.
95494.m: At the Saut du Doubs, the Doubs leaps into the depths.

95495.q: Which world-famous architect was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel in 1887?
95495.e: Le Corbusier's real name was Charles-Édouard Jeanneret, and he grew up in La Chaux-de-Fonds. He became one of the most important architects of the 20th century.
95495.m: Le Corbusier came from La Chaux-de-Fonds.

95496.q: Which famous racing driver and car maker was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1878?
95496.e: Louis Chevrolet emigrated to the USA, where he co-founded the Chevrolet car brand. He was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds.
95496.m: Chevrolet has its roots in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

95497.q: Since which year has Neuchâtel been a canton of the Swiss Confederation?
95497.e: Neuchâtel was admitted to the Confederation as a canton in 1815. At the same time, until 1848 it remained a principality of the King of Prussia.
95497.m: Neuchâtel has been a Swiss canton since 1815.

95498.q: Why is 1 March a public holiday in the canton of Neuchâtel?
a: It commemorates the founding of the Republic of Neuchâtel in 1848
It commemorates the invention of the wristwatch
The grape harvest begins on this day
95498.e: On 1 March 1848, the people of Neuchâtel declared a republic. The canton has celebrated this day every year since.
95498.m: On 1 March, Neuchâtel celebrates its republic.

95499.q: Which museum in La Chaux-de-Fonds shows clocks and watches from many centuries?
95499.e: The Musée international d'horlogerie in La Chaux-de-Fonds shows thousands of clocks and watches. There you learn how timekeeping developed.
95499.m: The International Museum of Horology is in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

95500.q: What are the famous Jaquet-Droz figures displayed in the museum in Neuchâtel?
a: Automatons that can write, draw and play music
95500.e: In the 18th century, Pierre Jaquet-Droz and his assistants built three mechanical dolls: the Writer, the Draughtsman and the Musician. They still work today.
95500.m: The Jaquet-Droz automatons write, draw and play music.

95501.q: Which river has carved a wild gorge in the canton of Neuchâtel, with a popular footpath running through it?
95501.e: The Areuse flows from the Val-de-Travers to Lake Neuchâtel. In the Gorges de l'Areuse, paths lead over bridges and along rock walls.
95501.m: The Areuse flows through a wild gorge.

95502.q: Which two lakes is Lake Neuchâtel connected to by canals?
a: Lake Geneva and Lac de Joux
95502.e: Lake Neuchâtel, Lake Biel and Lake Murten together form the Three Lakes Region. Canals link the three lakes.
95502.m: Lake Neuchâtel, Lake Biel and Lake Murten form the Three Lakes Region.

95508.q: What is special about the “CabriO” cable car up the Stanserhorn in Nidwalden?
a: It has an open upper deck
95508.e: The CabriO is a cable car with two floors. On the open upper deck you ride up the Stanserhorn under the open sky.
95508.m: On the CabriO you ride up the Stanserhorn with no roof above you.

95509.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Nidwalden?
95509.e: People in Nidwalden speak German, and in everyday life the Nidwalden dialect. The canton lies in Central Switzerland.

95510.q: Which lake is the canton of Nidwalden on?
95510.e: Nidwalden lies on the southern shore of Lake Lucerne. Places such as Hergiswil, Buochs and Beckenried are right by the water.

95511.q: What can you see on the coat of arms of the canton of Nidwalden?
a: A white double key on a red background
A black bear on a white background
A bull's head on a yellow background
An ibex on a white background
95511.e: The coat of arms of Nidwalden shows a white double key on a red background. The key is the symbol of Saint Peter.
95511.m: Nidwalden has a white double key on red.

95512.q: Which traditional festival of the Alpine herders is celebrated in Nidwalden in autumn?
95512.e: At the Älplerchilbi, the Alpine herders give thanks for a good summer on the mountain pastures. There is a parade, music and funny rhymes.
95512.m: In autumn, Nidwalden celebrates the Älplerchilbi.

95513.q: What is made at the Glasi in Hergiswil in the canton of Nidwalden?
95513.e: At the Glasi Hergiswil, glass is blown by hand. Visitors can watch.

95514.q: Which mountain rises directly above the village of Stans in Nidwalden?
95514.e: The Stanserhorn towers up just behind Stans. From the summit you can see many lakes and mountains of Central Switzerland.

95515.q: What does the company Pilatus build in Stans in the canton of Nidwalden?
95515.e: Pilatus Aircraft in Stans builds planes that are sold all over the world. The company is an important employer in Nidwalden.
95515.m: Pilatus planes are built in Stans.

95516.q: Roughly how high is the Stanserhorn in Nidwalden?
95516.e: The Stanserhorn is 1,898 metres high. You can get up by an old funicular and the CabriO.
95516.m: The Stanserhorn is just under 1,900 metres high.

95517.q: Which river flows through Nidwalden and into Lake Lucerne at Buochs?
95517.e: The Engelberger Aa comes from the Engelberg valley and flows through Nidwalden. At Buochs it flows into Lake Lucerne.
95517.m: The Engelberger Aa is the main river of Nidwalden.

95518.q: Which long motorway tunnel connects Nidwalden with the canton of Uri?
95518.e: The Seelisberg Tunnel on the A2 motorway runs from Beckenried in Nidwalden to Seedorf in Uri. It is about 9 kilometres long.
95518.m: Through the Seelisberg Tunnel you drive from Nidwalden to Uri.

95519.q: Which lake does the car ferry from Beckenried in Nidwalden to Gersau in the canton of Schwyz cross?
95519.e: The car ferry links Beckenried in Nidwalden with Gersau in the canton of Schwyz. This saves a long detour around Lake Lucerne.
95519.m: The ferry goes back and forth across Lake Lucerne.

95520.q: What is the name of the skiing and hiking area above Beckenried in Nidwalden?
95520.e: An aerial cableway runs from Beckenried up to the Klewenalp. In winter people ski there, and in summer they hike with a view of the lake.

95521.q: What is the Hammetschwand Lift on the Bürgenstock in Nidwalden?
a: An outdoor lift on a steep rock face
A suspension bridge over a gorge
95521.e: The Hammetschwand Lift travels more than 150 metres up the outside of a rock face. It is considered the highest outdoor lift in Europe. At the top there is a great view of Lake Lucerne.
95521.m: On the Bürgenstock, a lift climbs up the outside of the rock face.

95522.q: With which two lands did Unterwalden, which Nidwalden was part of, form the alliance in 1291?
95522.e: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are the three founding cantons. Their alliance of 1291 is seen as the beginning of the Swiss Confederation.
95522.m: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are the founding cantons.

95523.q: Which railway connects Lucerne with Engelberg via Stans?
95523.e: The Zentralbahn runs from Lucerne through Nidwalden via Stans to Engelberg. Its trains run on narrow-gauge tracks.
95523.m: The Zentralbahn takes you from Lucerne via Stans to Engelberg.

95530.q: What is the capital of the canton of Obwalden?
95530.e: The capital of Obwalden is Sarnen. The town lies at the northern end of Lake Sarnen.

95531.q: On which lake does Sarnen, the capital of Obwalden, lie?
95531.e: Sarnen lies on Lake Sarnen. In summer the lake is popular for swimming and rowing.

95532.q: What can you see on the coat of arms of the canton of Obwalden?
a: A key on red and white
95532.e: The coat of arms of Obwalden is red at the top and white at the bottom. On it is a double key, each part in the opposite colour.
95532.m: Obwalden: red on top, white below, with a key.

95533.q: Which high mountain with a glacier lies near Engelberg in Obwalden?
95533.e: The Titlis is over 3,200 metres high and has a glacier. There is snow up there even in summer.

95534.q: What is special about the “Rotair” cable car up the Titlis near Engelberg?
a: The cabin rotates during the ride
It is powered by muscle strength
95534.e: The Rotair cabin turns once all the way round during the ride. That way every passenger sees the mountains all around.
95534.m: In the Rotair, the cabin turns in a circle.

95535.q: What can you watch at the show dairy at Engelberg Abbey in Obwalden?
95535.e: At the Engelberg Abbey show dairy, you look through glass windows to see how milk becomes cheese. You can buy the cheese right there.
95535.m: Cheese is made at Engelberg Abbey.

95536.q: Which pass takes you from Obwalden to the Bernese Oberland?
95536.e: The Brünig Pass connects Obwalden with the Hasli valley in the Bernese Oberland. A road and a railway line cross it.
95536.m: The Brünig takes you from Obwalden to Bern.

95537.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Obwalden?
95537.e: People in Obwalden speak German, and in everyday life the Obwalden dialect. The canton belongs to Central Switzerland.

95538.q: In which gorge in Obwalden did Brother Klaus live as a hermit?
95538.e: Nicholas of Flüe withdrew to the Ranft, a gorge below Flüeli. He lived there for many years in a small cell.
95538.m: Brother Klaus lived in the Ranft.

95539.q: Which winter sports World Cup takes place in Engelberg every December?
95539.e: On the Gross-Titlis ski jump in Engelberg, the best ski jumpers in the world compete every December. Thousands of fans watch.
95539.m: In Engelberg the ski jumpers fly.

95540.q: Which monks have lived in Engelberg Abbey in Obwalden since the 12th century?
95540.e: Engelberg Abbey was founded in 1120. Since then, monks have lived there according to the Rule of Saint Benedict.

95541.q: How many municipalities does the canton of Obwalden have?
95541.e: Obwalden has seven municipalities: Sarnen, Kerns, Sachseln, Alpnach, Giswil, Lungern and Engelberg.

95542.q: In which place in Obwalden does the Pilatus Railway, the steepest cogwheel railway in the world, start?
95542.e: The Pilatus Railway runs from Alpnachstad on Lake Alpnach up Mount Pilatus. It has a gradient of up to 48 per cent.
95542.m: The steepest cogwheel railway starts in Alpnachstad.

95543.q: What is the name of the holiday and ski resort with a mountain lake high above the Melchtal in Obwalden?
95543.e: At Melchsee-Frutt, Lake Melch lies at almost 1,900 metres. In summer people hike, and in winter they ski.

95544.q: Which river connects Lake Sarnen with Lake Alpnach in Obwalden?
95544.e: The Sarner Aa flows out of Lake Sarnen through Sarnen. It flows into Lake Alpnach, part of Lake Lucerne.
95544.m: The Sarner Aa flows from Lake Sarnen to Lake Alpnach.

95545.q: What takes place every summer on the Brünig Pass between Obwalden and Bern?
95545.e: At the Brünig Schwinget, the best Swiss wrestlers from Central Switzerland and the Bernese Oberland compete. The festival is very popular.
95545.m: There is Swiss wrestling on the Brünig.

95552.q: What is the capital of the canton of St Gallen?
95552.e: The capital has the same name as the canton: St Gallen. The cantonal government and the cantonal parliament work there.
95552.m: Canton of St Gallen, capital St Gallen.

95553.q: Which town in the canton of St Gallen is called the “Town of Roses”?
95553.e: In Rapperswil on Lake Zurich, thousands of roses bloom in several gardens. That is why the town is called the “Town of Roses”.
95553.m: Rapperswil on Lake Zurich is the Town of Roses.

95554.q: Which sausage is a famous speciality from the canton of St Gallen?
95554.e: The white St Gallen bratwurst, made mainly from veal, is known all over Switzerland. Many people from St Gallen like it best with a Bürli bread roll and without mustard.
95554.m: People like to eat the St Gallen bratwurst with a Bürli roll.

95555.q: On which large lake does the St Gallen town of Rorschach lie?
95555.e: Rorschach lies on the shore of Lake Constance. In the north, the canton of St Gallen has a share of this large lake.

95556.q: Which river forms the border between the canton of St Gallen and Austria?
95556.e: The Rhine flows through the St Gallen Rhine Valley. On one side is Switzerland, on the other side Austria.
95556.m: In the Rhine Valley, the Rhine separates St Gallen from Austria.

95557.q: Which small country borders the canton of St Gallen?
95557.e: The Principality of Liechtenstein lies right next to the canton of St Gallen, on the other side of the Rhine.
95557.m: Liechtenstein is St Gallen's small neighbour.

95558.q: Which big fair takes place in the city of St Gallen every autumn?
95558.e: The OLMA is a big fair for farming and food. The animals and the piglet race are especially popular.
95558.m: In autumn it is OLMA time in St Gallen.

95559.q: Which two cantons are completely surrounded by the canton of St Gallen?
95559.e: The two Appenzells lie like an island in the middle of the canton of St Gallen. All around them is St Gallen territory.
95559.m: St Gallen surrounds the two Appenzells.

95560.q: Which lake lies between the canton of St Gallen and the canton of Glarus?
95560.e: Lake Walen lies between steep mountains. The northern shore belongs to the canton of St Gallen, and part of the southern shore to the canton of Glarus.
95560.m: Lake Walen lies between St Gallen and Glarus.

95561.q: What is the name of the mountain range with seven peaks above Lake Walen in the canton of St Gallen?
95561.e: The Churfirsten are a row of seven peaks. From Lake Walen you see their steep rock faces, and from the Toggenburg gentle meadow slopes.

95562.q: Through which valley in the canton of St Gallen does the Thur flow?
95562.e: The Thur rises in the upper Toggenburg and flows through the Toggenburg. The valley is known for hiking, skiing and its folk music.
95562.m: The Thur flows through the Toggenburg.

95563.q: Which spa resort in the canton of St Gallen is known for its warm thermal water?
95563.e: In Bad Ragaz you bathe in warm thermal water. The water comes from the nearby Tamina Gorge.
95563.m: Bad Ragaz has warm thermal water from the Tamina Gorge.

95564.q: What is the University of St Gallen (HSG) especially known for?
95564.e: The University of St Gallen is one of the best-known universities in Europe for economics and business. Students from many countries go there.
95564.m: The HSG is a university for business and economics.

95565.q: Which of these cantons does NOT border the canton of St Gallen?
95565.e: St Gallen borders Thurgau, Zurich, Schwyz, Glarus, the Grisons and the two Appenzells. Lucerne lies further west.
95565.m: St Gallen has seven neighbouring cantons, and Lucerne is not one of them.

95566.q: Which skiing and hiking area in the canton of St Gallen lies high above Lake Walen?
95566.e: Flumserberg lies on the south side above Lake Walen. From there you look straight across at the Churfirsten.
95566.m: From Flumserberg you look out over Lake Walen and the Churfirsten.

95567.q: Which square in the city of St Gallen is covered with a red surface and looks like a huge open-air living room?
95567.e: The City Lounge in the Bleicheli district is covered with red plastic, even the benches and a table. The artist Pipilotti Rist helped to design it.
95567.m: The City Lounge in St Gallen is a red living room under the open sky.

95574.q: What is the capital of the canton of Schaffhausen?
95574.e: The capital has the same name as the canton: Schaffhausen. The town lies right on the Rhine.

95575.q: Which neighbouring country surrounds the canton of Schaffhausen on almost all sides?
95575.e: The canton of Schaffhausen is almost completely surrounded by Germany. Only in the south does it border the cantons of Zurich and Thurgau.
95575.m: Schaffhausen is surrounded by Germany almost everywhere.

95576.q: On which river does the town of Schaffhausen lie?
95576.e: The town of Schaffhausen lies on the Rhine. In the past, boats had to unload their goods here because the Rhine Falls blocked the way further downstream.

95577.q: Which little town in the canton of Schaffhausen is famous for its colourfully painted house fronts?
95577.e: In the old town of Stein am Rhein, many houses are painted with colourful pictures. The little town is one of the most beautiful in Switzerland.
95577.m: Stein am Rhein has painted houses.

95578.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Schaffhausen?
95578.e: On the Schaffhausen coat of arms, a black ram leaps on a yellow background. The ram (in German Schafbock) suits the name “Schaffhausen”.
95578.m: Schaffhausen has a ram on its coat of arms.

95579.q: What is a “Bölletünne”, a speciality from Schaffhausen?
95579.e: In the local dialect, “Bölle” means onion and “Tünne” is a flat tart. So the Bölletünne is a tasty onion tart.

95580.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Schaffhausen?
95580.e: People in the canton of Schaffhausen speak German, and in everyday life mostly the Schaffhausen dialect.

95581.q: As far as which lake can you travel by boat on the Rhine from Schaffhausen?
95581.e: From Schaffhausen, boats travel up the Rhine via Stein am Rhein to the Untersee, part of Lake Constance. The trip is considered one of the most beautiful river journeys in Europe.
95581.m: From Schaffhausen you can take a boat to Lake Constance.

95582.q: What is special about the location of the canton of Schaffhausen?
a: Most of it lies north of the Rhine
It lies entirely in the Alps
It has no border with another country
95582.e: Almost the whole canton of Schaffhausen lies on the northern side of the Rhine. That is unusual in Switzerland.
95582.m: Schaffhausen lies almost entirely north of the Rhine.

95583.q: At what time does the little Munot bell in Schaffhausen ring every evening?
95583.e: Every evening at 9 pm, the little bell on the Munot rings. In the past it was a sign that the town gates were being closed.
95583.m: The little Munot bell rings at nine in the evening.

95584.q: In which year did Schaffhausen join the Swiss Confederation?
95584.e: Schaffhausen became a member of the Confederation in 1501. Basel joined in the same year.

95585.q: Which two Swiss cantons does the canton of Schaffhausen border?
95585.e: Schaffhausen has only two neighbouring cantons: Zurich and Thurgau. All its other borders are with Germany.
95585.m: Schaffhausen's neighbouring cantons are Zurich and Thurgau.

95586.q: In which Schaffhausen municipality is the Rhine Falls?
95586.e: The Rhine Falls is at Neuhausen am Rheinfall, right next to the town of Schaffhausen. The other bank, with Laufen Castle, belongs to the canton of Zurich.
95586.m: The Rhine Falls is at Neuhausen.

95587.q: Which well-known watch brand has its headquarters in the town of Schaffhausen?
95587.e: The watch company IWC was founded in Schaffhausen in 1868 by an American. It still makes expensive watches there today.

95588.q: What is the name of the wooded hill area of Jura limestone in the canton of Schaffhausen?
95588.e: The Randen is an outlier of the Jura in the canton of Schaffhausen. It is a popular hiking area with lookout towers.
95588.m: The Randen is the Schaffhausen Jura.

95595.q: What is the capital of the canton of Schwyz?
95595.e: The capital has the same name as the canton: Schwyz. It lies at the foot of the two Mythen peaks.

95596.q: What are the two pointed mountain peaks above the town of Schwyz called?
95596.e: The Grosser Mythen and the Kleiner Mythen are the landmark of Schwyz. A steep path leads up the Grosser Mythen.
95596.m: The two Mythen stand above Schwyz.

95597.q: Which famous monastery is in the canton of Schwyz?
95597.e: The Benedictine abbey of Einsiedeln is over 1,000 years old. Many pilgrims go there every year.
95597.m: Einsiedeln Abbey is in the canton of Schwyz.

95598.q: Which world-famous pocket knife is made in the canton of Schwyz?
a: The Swiss Army Knife by Victorinox
95598.e: The company Victorinox makes red pocket knives in Ibach near Schwyz. They are sold all over the world.
95598.m: The red pocket knife comes from Schwyz.

95599.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Schwyz look like?
a: Red with a small white cross at the top left
White with a red cross in the middle
95599.e: The Schwyz coat of arms is completely red. At the top left there is a small white cross.
95599.m: Schwyz: red with a small white cross.

95600.q: Which group of cantons does Schwyz belong to, together with Uri and Unterwalden?
a: The border cantons on the Rhine
95600.e: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are called the founding cantons. According to tradition, they were the first to join together, in 1291.
95600.m: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are the founding cantons.

95601.q: Which baked treat is a speciality from Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz?
95601.e: Einsiedler Schafböcke are honey gingerbread biscuits. They are shaped in wooden moulds, often with the picture of a ram.

95602.q: Which big reservoir lies near Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz?
95602.e: Lake Sihl was dammed about 90 years ago. Its water is used to make electricity, and in summer you can swim in it.
95602.m: Lake Sihl is the largest reservoir in Switzerland.

95603.q: Which famous figure do pilgrims honour in the abbey church of Einsiedeln?
95603.e: In the Chapel of Grace in the abbey church there is a statue of Mary with a dark face, the Black Madonna. It is the goal of many pilgrimages.
95603.m: The Black Madonna is in Einsiedeln.

95604.q: Which mountain, often called the “Queen of the Mountains”, lies partly in the canton of Schwyz?
95604.e: The Rigi lies between Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and Lake Lauerz. Its summit, Rigi Kulm, belongs to the canton of Schwyz.
95604.m: The Rigi is the Queen of the Mountains.

95605.q: What is the name of the huge cave in the Muota valley that is one of the longest cave systems in the world?
95605.e: The Hölloch in the Muota valley is more than 200 kilometres long. Researchers are still discovering new passages there.
95605.m: The Hölloch is one of the longest caves in the world.

95606.q: What are the men from the Muota valley who forecast the weather using nature called?
95606.e: The Muotatal Wetterschmöcker watch things like ants, fir cones or clouds. Twice a year they forecast the weather for the next six months.
95606.m: The Wetterschmöcker read the weather from nature.

95607.q: Which battle took place in 1315 on the border between today's cantons of Schwyz and Zug?
95607.e: At Morgarten in 1315, the Confederates defeated a Habsburg army. Afterwards Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden renewed their alliance.
95607.m: The Battle of Morgarten was in 1315.

95608.q: Which animal park in the canton of Schwyz lies on the site of an old landslide?
95608.e: Goldau Animal Park lies among huge boulders that crashed down from the Rossberg in a landslide. Native animals such as deer, bears and wolves live there.
95608.m: Goldau Animal Park lies in a landslide area.

95609.q: On which lake does Pfäffikon in the canton of Schwyz lie?
95609.e: Pfäffikon lies on the southern shore of Lake Zurich in the Höfe region. So the canton of Schwyz borders several large lakes.
95609.m: Pfäffikon SZ lies on Lake Zurich.

95610.q: Which of these cantons does NOT border the canton of Schwyz?
95610.e: Schwyz borders Uri, Zug, Lucerne, Zurich, St Gallen and Glarus, among others. Bern lies much further west.
95610.m: Schwyz has many neighbours, but Bern is not one of them.

95617.q: What is the capital of the canton of Thurgau?
95617.e: The capital of Thurgau is Frauenfeld. It is also the largest town in the canton.
95617.m: The capital of Thurgau is Frauenfeld.

95618.q: Which river is the canton of Thurgau named after?
95618.e: The Thur flows right across the canton. Thurgau takes its name from it.
95618.m: Thurgau is named after the Thur.

95619.q: Which country lies on the other side of Lake Constance, opposite Thurgau?
95619.e: Germany lies on the other side of Lake Constance. Near Kreuzlingen, Thurgau also borders Germany directly on land.

95620.q: Which animals can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Thurgau?
95620.e: On the Thurgau coat of arms, two yellow lions stride one above the other. The background is divided diagonally into white and green.
95620.m: There are two lions on the Thurgau coat of arms.

95621.q: Which Thurgau town borders the German city of Konstanz directly?
95621.e: Kreuzlingen and Konstanz have grown together. You can walk from Switzerland into Germany.

95622.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Thurgau?
95622.e: People in Thurgau speak German, and in everyday life mostly the Thurgau dialect.

95623.q: Which of these cantons is a neighbour of the canton of Thurgau?
95623.e: Thurgau borders St Gallen, Zurich and Schaffhausen. The other cantons are far away.
95623.m: St Gallen is a neighbour of Thurgau.

95624.q: Which is the largest town in the canton of Thurgau?
95624.e: Frauenfeld is both the capital and the largest town. Kreuzlingen on Lake Constance comes a close second.
95624.m: Frauenfeld is the largest town in Thurgau.

95625.q: In which year did Thurgau become a canton of the Confederation in its own right?
95625.e: With Napoleon's Act of Mediation, Thurgau became a canton with equal rights in 1803. St Gallen, Aargau, Ticino, Vaud and the Grisons joined in the same year.
95625.m: Thurgau has been a canton since 1803.

95626.q: Which former monastery near Frauenfeld is now a place with museums, a hotel and its own farm?
95626.e: Carthusian monks used to live in the Ittingen Charterhouse. Today there is an art museum, a hotel, gardens and a farm estate.
95626.m: The Ittingen Charterhouse was a monastery and is now a cultural centre.

95627.q: Which drinks company in Arbon in the canton of Thurgau is known for its apple juice?
95627.e: The Möhl cider press in Arbon has been pressing Thurgau apples into apple juice for many decades. That suits the apple canton of Thurgau.
95627.m: Möhl in Arbon makes apple juice.

95628.q: Which big music festival takes place in Frauenfeld every summer?
95628.e: The Openair Frauenfeld is one of the biggest hip-hop festivals in Europe. It takes place on the Grosse Allmend.
95628.m: A big open-air festival happens in Frauenfeld every summer.

95629.q: From which Thurgau harbour does a car ferry cross Lake Constance to Friedrichshafen in Germany?
95629.e: The ferry links Romanshorn with Friedrichshafen. It carries people, bicycles and cars.
95629.m: The ferry goes from Romanshorn to Friedrichshafen.

95630.q: Which thin, rolled wafer biscuit comes from Gottlieben in the canton of Thurgau?
95630.e: Gottlieber Hüppen are crispy wafer rolls, often filled with chocolate or praline. Gottlieben lies on the Seerhein between Lake Constance and the Untersee.
95630.m: Gottlieber Hüppen are wafer rolls from Thurgau.

95631.q: What colours is the background of the Thurgau coat of arms?
95631.e: The Thurgau coat of arms is divided diagonally, white at the top and green at the bottom. On each part there is a yellow lion.
95631.m: Thurgau: white and green with two lions.

95638.q: What is the capital of the canton of Ticino?
95638.e: Many people think of Lugano, but the capital is Bellinzona. That is also where the three famous castles stand.
95638.m: The capital of Ticino is Bellinzona, not Lugano.

95639.q: Which is the largest town in the canton of Ticino?
95639.e: Lugano on Lake Lugano is the largest town in Ticino. It is an important centre for banking, tourism and culture.
95639.m: Lugano is the largest town in Ticino.

95640.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Ticino border?
95640.e: Ticino juts southwards like a wedge and is surrounded by Italy on almost three sides.

95641.q: On which large lake does the Ticino town of Locarno lie?
95641.e: Locarno lies at the northern end of Lake Maggiore. Most of this lake belongs to Italy.

95642.q: Which fruit used to be so important in Ticino that its tree was called the “bread tree”?
95642.e: In the past, people in Ticino ate lots of chestnuts in winter, for example dried or as flour. Today hot roasted chestnuts are very popular in autumn.
95642.m: The chestnut was Ticino's bread tree.

95643.q: Where in Ticino can you see the whole of Switzerland in miniature, with models of houses, railways and mountains?
a: At the Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne
95643.e: Swissminiatur in Melide on Lake Lugano shows more than a hundred models of famous Swiss buildings. Little trains run through the park.
95643.m: In Melide, Switzerland stands in miniature.

95644.q: What colours is the coat of arms of the canton of Ticino?
95644.e: The Ticino coat of arms is divided vertically: red on the left and blue on the right.

95645.q: What nickname does Ticino have because of its warm, sunny weather?
95645.e: The sun often shines in Ticino, and it is warmer than north of the Alps. That is why even palm trees grow there.
95645.m: Ticino is the sun lounge of Switzerland.

95646.q: Which railway tunnel runs from Erstfeld in the canton of Uri to Bodio in Ticino and is the longest railway tunnel in the world?
95646.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is 57 kilometres long and opened in 2016. Trains can travel much faster from the north to Ticino through it.
95646.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is 57 kilometres long.

95647.q: In which year did Ticino become a canton of Switzerland in its own right?
95647.e: With Napoleon's Act of Mediation, Ticino became a canton in 1803. Before that, it was ruled as a subject territory by other cantons.
95647.m: Ticino has been a canton since 1803.

95648.q: Which prize is awarded for the best film at the Locarno Film Festival?
95648.e: At the Locarno Film Festival in August, films are shown in the open air on the Piazza Grande. The main prize is the Golden Leopard, in Italian “Pardo d'oro”.
95648.m: In Locarno you win the Golden Leopard.

95649.q: Which Ticino valley is known for its crystal-clear green water and the old stone bridge Ponte dei Salti?
95649.e: The Verzasca flows through a wild valley with green, very clear water. At Lavertezzo, the double-arched Ponte dei Salti spans the river.
95649.m: The Ponte dei Salti is in the Verzasca Valley.

95650.q: Which well-known pilgrimage church sits on a rock high above Locarno?
95650.e: The church of Madonna del Sasso stands on a rock above Locarno. You can walk up or take a funicular.
95650.m: The Madonna del Sasso stands above Locarno.

95651.q: Which of these cantons borders the canton of Ticino?
95651.e: Ticino has three neighbouring cantons: Valais, Uri and the Grisons. All its other borders are with Italy.
95651.m: Ticino borders Valais, Uri and the Grisons.

95658.q: What is the capital of the canton of Uri?
95658.e: Altdorf is the capital of Uri. The government and the cantonal parliament meet there.

95659.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Uri?
95659.e: The Uri coat of arms shows a black bull's head with a red nose ring on a yellow background. It is called the Uri bull.
95659.m: The Uri bull looks out from the Uri coat of arms.

95660.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Uri?
95660.e: People in the canton of Uri speak German, or to be precise the Uri dialect, a form of Swiss German.

95661.q: Which famous legendary hero is said to have come from Bürglen in the canton of Uri?
95661.e: According to legend, William Tell came from Bürglen. Today there is a Tell Museum there.
95661.m: According to legend, William Tell comes from Bürglen in Uri.

95662.q: Which river flows through the Reuss valley in Uri?
95662.e: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area and flows through the whole of Uri into Lake Uri.

95663.q: What is the part of Lake Lucerne that lies in the canton of Uri called?
95663.e: The southernmost arm of Lake Lucerne is called Lake Uri. It is surrounded by steep rock walls.
95663.m: Uri's part of the lake is called Lake Uri.

95664.q: On which famous meadow in the canton of Uri is the Rütli Oath said to have taken place?
95664.e: The Rütli lies on Lake Uri in the municipality of Seelisberg. Representatives of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are said to have sworn their alliance there.
95664.m: The Rütli lies in Uri on Lake Uri.

95665.q: Since when has the canton of Uri been part of the Confederation?
a: Since 1291; it is a founding canton
95665.e: Together with Schwyz and Unterwalden, Uri is one of the three founding cantons. The Federal Charter dates from 1291.
95665.m: Uri has been part of it since 1291 and is a founding canton.

95666.q: How long is the Gotthard Base Tunnel, whose north portal is near Erstfeld in the canton of Uri?
95666.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel opened in 2016 and is about 57 kilometres long. It is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
95666.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is about 57 kilometres long.

95667.q: Which pass connects the canton of Uri with the canton of Glarus?
95667.e: The Klausen Pass leads from Altdorf through the Schächental across to Linthal in the canton of Glarus.
95667.m: The Klausen takes you from Uri to Glarus.

95668.q: Which pass connects the canton of Uri with the canton of the Grisons?
